key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
engineering_relevance: Combining complementary optical, electrical, and barrier functions offers a route to more efficient and durable planar hybrid solar cells.
method: Fabricate planar PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si Schottky junctions on untextured substrates.
Benchmark against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Evaluate optoelectronic performance and efficiency retention after 75 days of ambient exposure.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish multi-year outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale performance.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
